source_evidence: Unlike traditional mutual funds (or “open-end funds”), they are not required to buy back shares from shareholders.
question: Misconception: Publicly traded closed-end funds must buy back shares from shareholders just like traditional mutual funds.
answer: Correction: Publicly traded closed-end funds are not required to buy back their shares. After their public offering, their shares trade on national securities exchanges at market prices, which may be above or below the value of the fund’s underlying investments.
